title: pluggable constrained-sampling backends (CFG + regex) and tokenizer-safety for structured output
author: Miguel Torres
release_notes: Introduces a pluggable constrained-sampling backend API with two reference backends (CFG-based grammar engine and a lightweight regex engine), plus a tokenizer-safety layer to avoid broken constraints across subtoken boundaries. Streaming behavior when constraints are active is improved with incremental validator checkpoints. No public-breaking changes to the user-facing structured_output API, but operator-configured constraint behavior may change some edge-case outputs.
description:
Motivation: Customers using structured output and function/tool calling request more robust, composable constraint support beyond the current monolithic implementation. Existing constrained-decoding broke streaming stability in several cases (constraints spanning token boundaries, long-regex patterns, and ambiguous CFG rules). This PR introduces a pluggable constrained-sampling backend interface and two reference implementations (CFG and regex) plus a tokenizer-safety layer to prevent constraint logic from being invalidated by tokenizer splits. Summary of changes: adds a ConstrainedBackend interface, implements GrammarBackend (nearley-inspired runtime) and RegexBackend (incremental DFA checks), introduces TokenizerSafety middleware to normalize constraints vs tokenizer tokenization, updates the OpenAI-compat layer to surface constraint errors early, and adds end-to-end streaming tests and benchmarks. Compatibility notes: Default behavior preserves existing runtime semantics when no constraints are supplied; operators can opt into the new backends via config. Streaming notes: validators now run incrementally on partial tokens and on new decoder tokens; when a backend signals impossible constraints we gracefully emit a structured error and fallback to the configured policy (fallback_model or unconstrained decode). Security and perf: RegexBackend compiles patterns to bounded DFAs and enforces a max-state budget to avoid exponential blowups; GrammarBackend compiles to a guarded form with a static limit on lookahead. Tests: unit + integration + new e2e tests for streaming + tokenizer edge cases. Linear tickets: ENG-1248 (pluggable constrained backends), ENG-1302 (tokenizer-safety for constraint validation).

review_comments: Aisha Khan: Can the GrammarBackend handle left-recursive rules? If not, add a guard or preprocessor to reject or transform left recursion.
Miguel Torres: GrammarBackend uses a guarded LL variant; left recursion is rejected at compile time with a clear error suggesting refactor or using the regex backend for the pattern.
Liam O'Connor: RegexBackend looks good but we need to ensure denial-of-service vectors are mitigated. Add a state_budget and fallback behavior. Also add a benchmark for pathological patterns.
Miguel Torres: Added state_budget config and CI job that runs the budgeted workloads. Default budget is conservative and documented in README.
Sofia Martinez: Streaming validator checkpoints add CPU overhead — did you measure end-to-end latency impact for small prompts?

Miguel Torres: Benchmarks show ~5-8% p99 token latency increase in worst-case when constraints are active; offline caching and short-circuiting reduce the impact for simple constraints. Added results to benchmarks/README.md.
Aisha Khan: Please add integration tests where a function call is triggered mid-constraint (edge case).
Miguel Torres: Added e2e test that interleaves a function call trigger and constraint enforcement; validated behavior is deterministic and falls back per config.
benchmark_results: Local benchmark (A100): GrammarBackend median token latency +3.1% vs baseline when constraints active; p99 +6.4%
Local benchmark (T4/low mem): RegexBackend median +2.8%, p99 +8.9% for very complex patterns; state_budget reduced p99 to +4.0%
Throughput: with batching enabled, constrained overhead amortizes and throughput drop <5% for typical prompt distributions used in our corpus
